items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: So we worked together quite a while. That was 1925 when he came back to work with us.

ctx.x: And Boots and his buddies, too, over there in the thirties. I guess that was a good swing band. Uh-huh. Um, when did you first meet Wingy?

Well, I was with Doc Bross, and we were working out of Albuquerque, New Mexico. And he came through there, and, uh, you know, the trains used to stop for lunch in Albuquerque. And I was living in a hotel right across from the station, and he heard, he'd heard about me. So, during this 30-minute lunch period, he came over to the hotel and looked me up. And this was, uh, about 1923 or something like that. And he was on his way out to join a fellow in Phoenix by the name of Ham Crawford. So I said, well, if you get…
Who was around New Orleans there?
